new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-09 (Board of County Commissioners unanimous adoption after a public hearing)
new_candidates.duration: One year from adoption (2026-07-09 to 2027-07-08), or until replaced sooner by permanent zoning
new_candidates.legal_basis: Interim zoning overlay resolution adopted unanimously by the Missoula County Board of County Commissioners on July 9, 2026, under Mont. Code Ann. Section 76-2-206
new_candidates.trigger: County commissioners directed to study an asserted emergency and possible mitigation measures related to data center development pressure in unincorporated county areas
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of the July 31, 2026 research date. Prohibits permitting new or expanded data centers in zoned and unzoned areas of unincorporated Missoula County outside the City of Missoula. Effective July 9, 2026; expires July 8, 2027, or sooner if replaced by permanent zoning. Adopted unanimously after a public hearing at which 30 members of the public spoke, all in support.
new_candidates.affected_projects: No specific named project identified in the captured record; applies prospectively countywide in unincorporated areas.
new_candidates.outcome: Enacted one-year interim zoning moratorium on new or expanded data centers in unincorporated Missoula County.

evidence.title: Data center interim zoning
evidence.supports: County's own account of the adopted interim zoning overlay: scope, effective date, and one-year term.

evidence.title: Missoula County adopts temporary moratorium on data centers
evidence.supports: Reports the unanimous commissioner vote following public comment from 30 speakers, all in support of the moratorium.

new_candidates.notes: The adopted resolution text is described as present in the July 9, 2026 agenda packet and official meeting minutes per the chronology's local capture references (research/_originals/missoula-county-bcc-2026-07-09-agenda-packet.pdf and .../minutes.pdf); those local captures were relied on for the legal basis and duration but are not independently retrievable web URLs, so only the two web-accessible sources are cited above as evidence. A June 29, 2026 announcement of the proposed pause is the same instrument's precursor step, not a separate event.
